title: 1.6 Biomimicry: More Examples from Nature
description: Additional well-known technologies imitated from nature (supplementary)

questions.question: The fastening technology of Velcro was inspired by ____.
options: the tiny hooks of burdock burrs that clung to a dog's fur
the smooth scales of a fish
the sticky web of a spider
the wax coating of a lotus leaf
questions.correctAnswer: the tiny hooks of burdock burrs that clung to a dog's fur

questions.question: Who invented Velcro by imitating nature?
The name Velcro is formed from the words ____.
The buoyancy control of submarines is inspired by ____.
options: the air bladder (swim bladder) of fish
questions.correctAnswer: the air bladder (swim bladder) of fish

questions.question: Sonar technology was developed by imitating the ____.
Dry adhesive tapes and climbing robots were inspired by the ability of geckos to ____.
options: climb smooth walls using microscopic bristles on their toes
change color to match their surroundings
release their tails to escape predators
questions.correctAnswer: climb smooth walls using microscopic bristles on their toes

questions.question: Gecko toe adhesion is explained by a force produced when the microscopic setae contact a surface, known as ____.
The self-cleaning property of the lotus leaf inspired ____.
The self-cleaning behaviour in which water drops roll off a surface and carry away dirt is called the ____.
More efficient wind turbine blades have been designed by imitating ____.
options: the tubercles (bumps) on humpback whale flippers
the smooth dorsal fin of a shark
questions.correctAnswer: the tubercles (bumps) on humpback whale flippers

questions.question: The hexagonal cells of beehives inspired ____.
The shape of beehive cells that saves material while giving strength is the ____.
More efficient LED lighting designs have been inspired by the ____.
The production of light by living organisms such as fireflies is called ____.
Drag-reducing swimsuit fabrics were inspired by the ____.
options: microscopic riblet structure of shark skin
questions.correctAnswer: microscopic riblet structure of shark skin

questions.question: Shark skin is covered with tiny tooth-like structures called ____.
Fog-harvesting nets and materials that collect water from air moisture were inspired by ____.
options: the Namib Desert beetle that collects water from fog on its back
the spines of a cactus only
questions.correctAnswer: the Namib Desert beetle that collects water from fog on its back

questions.question: Quieter aircraft and wind turbine blade designs were inspired by ____.
options: the fringed wing feathers of owls
questions.correctAnswer: the fringed wing feathers of owls

questions.question: The ability of owls to fly almost silently comes from ____.
options: special fringes on their wing feathers
downy body feathers that warm them
a dense layer of body fat
questions.correctAnswer: special fringes on their wing feathers

questions.question: Military camouflage patterns were inspired by ____.
options: the colour-changing and camouflage abilities of animals
the stripes of a zebra only
the spots of a leopard only
the fur of a polar bear only
questions.correctAnswer: the colour-changing and camouflage abilities of animals

questions.question: Agile drones and flapping-wing aircraft have been inspired by the flight of the ____.
The bright colours of butterfly wings are produced by ____.
options: nanostructures that create structural colour rather than pigments
coloured plant pigments they feed on
light absorbed from the sun only
questions.correctAnswer: nanostructures that create structural colour rather than pigments

questions.question: Structural colour produced by butterfly wing nanostructures has inspired ____.
Improved techniques for preserving live vaccines without constant refrigeration are inspired by ____.
Swarm robotics and optimization algorithms are inspired by ____.
options: the swarm behaviour of ant colonies
questions.correctAnswer: the swarm behaviour of ant colonies

questions.question: Impact-resistant helmets and shock-absorbing devices have been inspired by ____.
options: the ability of woodpeckers to absorb repeated impact without brain damage
the thick horn of a rhinoceros
the hard shell of a tortoise
the strong beak of a parrot
questions.correctAnswer: the ability of woodpeckers to absorb repeated impact without brain damage

questions.question: Solar thermal collectors that trap heat were inspired by ____.
options: the hollow translucent hairs of the polar bear that transmit heat to its black skin
the dark feathers of a raven
the heat-loving bacteria of hot springs
questions.correctAnswer: the hollow translucent hairs of the polar bear that transmit heat to its black skin

questions.question: Water-collection designs that pull moisture from the air were inspired by ____.
Research into ultra-light, strong synthetic materials has been guided by studying ____.
Velcro and drone swarms both demonstrate the principle that ____.
options: engineers solve problems by imitating nature's structures and behaviours
technology can only imitate large machines
animals learn new tools from scientists
questions.correctAnswer: engineers solve problems by imitating nature's structures and behaviours
